occurrences.description:
Come support our organization's mission of meeting essential needs of Native Americans and preserving cultural traditions, and experience the Pow Wow before or after your shift for free. Volunteer with the Native American Indian Association (NAIA) and our NAIA Food Booth for the 45th Annual Indian Education Tennessee Pow Wow the weekend of October 16, 17, and 18!  



Food booth volunteers are asked to:




	
help sell donated food and drink items 

	
assist in preparing food for volunteers and staff  

	
each shift is four hours

	
all volunteers will be provided with a meal for working their shift

	
may be asked to assist at other NAIA Booths and grounds cleanup

occurrences.opportunityName: Drive Change: Meal Delivery Volunteers Needed
occurrences.description:
Want to hit the road to make a difference? The Nashville Food Project is recruiting volunteers to deliver meals to our community partners across the city! Each week, TNFP distributes thousands of scratchmade meals with the support of our volunteer drivers. Volunteer drivers pick up meals from our kitchen and use our distribution vans to deliver to the nonprofits where they're served.



Daily Tasks Include




	
Loading TNFP delivery vehicles with the items needed for that day’s route

	
Pulling hot food from the ovens & recording the temperature of that hot food prior to departure on a route

	
Delivering meals to each TNFP partner site in a timely manner 

	
Note: Volunteers only deliver meals; they do not serve food or eat with our partner organizations.





Schedule Requirements



We’re seeking volunteers who can commit to recurring meal deliveries, either weekly, biweekly, or monthly. Can't commit to a shift? That's alright, we still encourage you to train with us and fill in for shifts where you can!



Registration



After expressing interest, our Volunteer Engagement Coordinator will reach out to schedule an orientation with our Food Access Team. "Expressing interest" on Hands On Nashville will not sign you up for this shift nor does our page on Hands On Nashville reflect the accurate number of spots available for any given shift.

occurrences.opportunityName: Free Grocery Distribution at Dream Streets West
occurrences.description:
Becoming a volunteer in our food ministry gives you the chance to meet people where they are and help to meet a basic need. You serve as a smiling face and welcoming spirit to all our community members.

 

Volunteers will help unload the food truck, organize the groceries so community members can "shop" for what they like, help community members carry the grocery box if needed, make community members feel welcome and valued and help with clean-up once the food site is over. 

 

Onboarding expectations:

It is standard procedure at Dream Streets for our volunteers 18 and older to complete a background check. You are required to complete this before starting any volunteer role. Because of the nature of our work and mobile accessibility in our communities of service, you may come in contact with a minor even if the position you are volunteering for is not student oriented. We will send the link in an email after you complete this sign-up. 

 

Dream Streets exists to protect and empower people living in distress. We serve individuals and families living in poverty in West and North Nashville through supplemental resources, wrap around services, and holistic support.

occurrences.opportunityName: Sort and Organize Donations - Rivergate Store
occurrences.description:
Sales from Thriftsmart's store benefit four nonprofits: Mercy Health Clinic, The Belize Project, African Leadership, and New Hope Academy.



Volunteers are needed to help sort donations, stock merchandise, color code and organize clothing on the sales floor, and organize shoes at the Thriftsmart store. If you have donations of clothing or shoes, Thriftsmart certainly welcomes your donation. All volunteers under the age of 18 are required to bring a signed Volunteer Release Form with them. 



Dress Code: Please wear clothing that is appropriate for a "family" oriented store. Shoes must be closed toe and no heel for your safety. Make sure to 'SIGN IN' in order to receive credit for coming.  



This project does NOT qualify for court-ordered community service hours. If you are needing to do community service hours please call our store number at (615)-833-8200 to speak with the volunteer coordinator, or go in person to speak to them.

occurrences.opportunityName: Seasonal Garden Prep
occurrences.description:
Community is an important part of the BELL Garden!  Join us as we prepare the garden for the current growing season. The garden serves as teaching and learning lab for volunteers, students of Bellevue Middle Prep, and our community!



The garden runs on volunteer power, no experience is necessary. Feel free to come just to learn more about gardening or share your experience.

 

Children under 12! If a parent or group will have children under the age of 12, please contact the opportunity leader below and let us know the ages in advance so we can plan activities that age group will enjoy. Children accompanying parents do not need to sign up for a spot.

 

Youth! If a group leader is signing up a group of youth under age 18, please contact the opportunity leader below before signing up.

 

As a volunteer, you may help:




	
Sow and harvest plants as needed

	
Water and weed existing garden rows

	
Prepare garden beds for planting

	
Spread wood chips around the garden





 

To prepare for volunteering:




	
Please wear closed toed shoes/boots and clothes you don't mind getting dirty.

	
We will also have all the tools you need.

	
We have a climate controlled classroom for breaks.

	
We do not cancel due to cold weather. The exception is snow or ice. Be safe!

	
Most of the garden is in full sun. Consider bringing a sunhat or visor.

	
Rain protection is suggested if rain is in the forecast. 

	
Most importantly: bring a water bottle, hydration is vital! We have a refrigerator to keep drinks cold.





 

Location:

Turn at our wooden sign and head down the drive that is marked ‘do not enter’ - this is only for when school is beginning and ending. Look for our green portable with our logo at the end of the drive.

 

About BELL Garden:

Founded in 2012, BELL Garden is a hybrid school and community garden located on the Bellevue Middle School Campus in Nashville, TN. As a 501(c)3 nonprofit, BELL Garden is focused on building healthier and deeper connected communities through garden based service, education, volunteerism, and food distribution to those in need.  The garden serves as a learning space for students, volunteers, and the community to grow food; learn about healthy eating choices; and gain an understanding of food access in our community.

occurrences.opportunityName: Hendersonville Samaritan Association - Daily Assistance
occurrences.description:
About Us

The Hendersonville Samaritan Association is the crisis assistance agency serving Hendersonville, Tennessee. Through the generosity of our community, 100% of the funds generated by our 8,000-square-foot Samaritan Thrift Store are reinvested directly into local families and individuals facing hardship.



Our ministry provides emergency food assistance through our food bank, crisis intake services, resource referrals, and financial assistance for qualifying residents. Every day, we work to connect people with the help, hope, and resources they need during difficult times.



Volunteers are the heart of our organization. Our daily operations depend on a dedicated team of volunteers working alongside paid staff to serve our neighbors in need.



Volunteer opportunities may include:


	
Sorting, organizing, and pricing donated merchandise

	
Assisting customers in our thrift store

	
Stocking shelves and organizing inventory

	
Helping process donations

	
Supporting food bank operations

	
Assisting with special events and seasonal drives

	
Administrative and office support

	
Welcoming visitors and helping connect clients with available resources



 

Impact

Every hour volunteered helps sustain programs that provide food, crisis assistance, and hope to Hendersonville families. By serving at HSA, volunteers become part of a mission that transforms donated goods into life-changing support for neighbors facing financial and personal challenges.



Volunteer Requirements


	
Friendly and positive attitude

	
Ability to work as part of a team

	
Commitment to serving others with dignity and compassion

	
No special experience required for most volunteer roles

	
Flexible scheduling available



 

Why Volunteer?

When you volunteer with Hendersonville Samaritan Association, you are doing more than serving in a thrift store—you are helping provide food for families, support for those in crisis, and connections to resources throughout our community.

occurrences.opportunityName: Grocery Volunteer
occurrences.description:
***PLEASE READ***

Expressing interest on our page on Hands On Nashville WILL NOT sign you up for this shift nor does our page on Hands On Nashville reflect the accurate number of spots available for any given shift. See below for more information about signing up.



SIGN UPS: We use our own website to organize sign-ups for our volunteer opportunities. After expressing interest, a staff member from The Store will reach out to send you a link to our official website where you will be able to sign up for your desired shifts. Please note that "expressing interest" on Hands On Nashville will not sign you up for this shift nor does our page on Hands On Nashville reflect the accurate number of spots available for any given shift. Official shift availability is listed on our website. If you’d like to plan a group volunteer day, please email volunteer@thestore.org and we’d be happy to help set something up! 



ABOUT: The Store operates as a year-round free grocery store allowing people to shop for their basic needs. There is no charge to those referred or to the people and agencies that send them. Our mission is to nourish communities and cultivate hope by providing nutritious food choices and access to supportive services in a dignified, loving environment. This volunteer opportunity will allow you to see your impact on the community in a real, tangible way. You will be helping provide wholesome food to families and individuals experiencing food insecurity in a welcoming environment that protects dignity and fosters hope.

 

ROLES: We are dependent on a volunteer base that is excited and passionate about building a better Nashville and Middle Tennessee. These volunteer shifts will mainly involve checking people out at the register, ensuring customers do not exceed specified item limits, bagging their groceries in a timely and efficient manner, and safely escorting customers to their vehicles with their groceries. At the start of the shift, you will have an orientation and brief training on our checkout system, so it is very important that you arrive on time. Roles will then be decided amongst volunteers and staff. During this shift you may also be greeting customers at check-in, helping people with questions while they shop, end of the day cleanup, maintaining store cleanliness throughout the day, stocking shelves/produce as needed, unloading pallets and other miscellaneous tasks as they arise. You will be able to take a break during your shift, so you are welcome to bring a snack and drink for break time. 

 

We truly appreciate your interest in supporting our mission, and we can't wait to work alongside you as we address food insecurity in the Nashville community!

occurrences.opportunityName: Artlink Studio Volunteer: Weekdays
occurrences.description:
ArtLink is a 501(c)(3) creative arts nonprofit in Clarksville, TN. We offer free and low-cost art projects and provide a welcoming, safe space for creative expression. Our mission is “To ignite passion and build character through creativity!”



Volunteers help create a welcoming and positive experience for everyone who visits ArtLink. Volunteers may assist with:




	
Assisting with studio opening tasks as directed by the Studio Lead

	
Welcoming patrons and helping create a friendly studio environment

	
Helping patrons get set up with art supplies

	
Helping participants with simple art projects and crafts

	
Assisting with basic studio organization and cleanup

	
Sweeping and tidying the studio

	
Organizing and restocking art supplies

	
Washing brushes and cleaning shared art materials

	
Helping with other light studio tasks as needed





Artistic experience is not necessary to volunteer with ArtLink. Our activities are simple, fun, and designed for everyone to enjoy. Whether you’re creative, crafty, or just enjoy helping others, there’s a place for you at ArtLink. If you have a particular artistic skill or creative interest, we’d also love to find ways to incorporate your talents when appropriate.



The most important thing is being willing to help, engage with our patrons, and contribute to a positive and creative environment.

occurrences.opportunityName: Over the Rainbow: Monica Ramey Sings The Music of Harold Arlen
occurrences.description:
In the next installment of her year-long residency at the Nashville Jazz Workshop, Monica Ramey presents a celebration of one of the Great American Songbook's most original composers — the man who gave the world Stormy Weather, Come Rain or Come Shine, and Over the Rainbow.



We need 3 volunteers to:      

Set up tables with tea lights      

Greet and seat guests 

Serve as hospitality floaters

Host concessions counter (canned beverages and snacks)    

Clean-up at end of performance      

 

Arrival: Volunteers are asked to arrive a few minutes before 6:00pm to huddle and receive specific event prep details and assignments.



Attire: Volunteers are asked to wear black/dark shirt, black/dark pants, black/dark shoes.  No logos, bright colors or baseball caps, please.



Performance: Volunteers are invited to attend and enjoy the performance 10 minutes after the event starts. 



Our Mission

The mission of the Nashville Jazz Workshop is to enrich people’s lives and build community through world class jazz education and performances. We accomplish our mission through a workshop environment where jazz professionals pass on their knowledge & experience in a journeyman/apprentice situation, classes for players & non-players, and performances to promote community appreciation of jazz.

occurrences.opportunityName: 45th Annual Education Pow Wow: Event Clean-Up
occurrences.description:
Come volunteer with the Native American Indian Association (NAIA) and help us maintain the Pow Wow grounds for our guests at our 45th Annual Indian Education Tennessee Pow Wow the weekend of October 16, 17, and 18! Each shift is 2-4 hours, and all volunteers will be provided with a meal for working their shift.  




	
Clean up volunteers are asked to help secure the arena performance stage at the close of each day of the Pow Wow. 

	
Clean up volunteers may be asked to help break down & secure the NAIA booths- Merchandise, Food Booth, Dancer Registration tent, Gate/Entrance

	
Clean up volunteers may be asked to help with maintaining/securing trash barrels and getting them ready for the next day's event

	
Volunteers may be asked to lift up to 50 pounds.

	
Post Pow-wow clean up will include breaking down tents, tables, A/V equipment, NAIA booth items, and helping with general grounds clean up.





Our organization was founded for and by Native Americans, and all executive board members are Native American. NAIA raises money to help Native Americans in Tennessee in need of assistance with food security, housing, employment, and education. The Annual Pow Wow is a celebration of Native American Cultures from all over the U.S., featuring Native American artisans, dancers, and storytellers.  



Come support our organization's mission of meeting essential needs of Native Americans and preserving cultural traditions, and experience Pow Wow before or after your shift for free.  



To learn more about Pow Wow and NAIA, please visit our website.

occurrences.opportunityName: Grocery Volunteer
occurrences.description:
***PLEASE READ***

Expressing interest on our page on Hands On Nashville WILL NOT sign you up for this shift nor does our page on Hands On Nashville reflect the accurate number of spots available for any given shift. See below for more information about signing up.



SIGN UPS: We use our own website to organize sign-ups for our volunteer opportunities. After expressing interest, a staff member from The Store will reach out to send you a link to our official website where you will be able to sign up for your desired shifts. Please note that "expressing interest" on Hands On Nashville will not sign you up for this shift nor does our page on Hands On Nashville reflect the accurate number of spots available for any given shift. Official shift availability is listed on our website. If you’d like to plan a group volunteer day, please email volunteer@thestore.org and we’d be happy to help set something up! 



ABOUT: The Store operates as a year-round free grocery store allowing people to shop for their basic needs. There is no charge to those referred or to the people and agencies that send them. Our mission is to nourish communities and cultivate hope by providing nutritious food choices and access to supportive services in a dignified, loving environment. This volunteer opportunity will allow you to see your impact on the community in a real, tangible way. You will be helping provide wholesome food to families and individuals experiencing food insecurity in a welcoming environment that protects dignity and fosters hope.

 

ROLES: We are dependent on a volunteer base that is excited and passionate about building a better Nashville and Middle Tennessee. These volunteer shifts will mainly involve checking people out at the register, ensuring customers do not exceed specified item limits, bagging their groceries in a timely and efficient manner, and safely escorting customers to their vehicles with their groceries. At the start of the shift, you will have an orientation and brief training on our checkout system, so it is very important that you arrive on time. Roles will then be decided amongst volunteers and staff. During this shift you may also be greeting customers at check-in, helping people with questions while they shop, end of the day cleanup, maintaining store cleanliness throughout the day, stocking shelves/produce as needed, unloading pallets and other miscellaneous tasks as they arise. You will be able to take a break during your shift, so you are welcome to bring a snack and drink for break time. 

 

We truly appreciate your interest in supporting our mission, and we can't wait to work alongside you as we address food insecurity in the Nashville community!

occurrences.opportunityName: Help Take Care of Goats! Goat Guardians 2026-2027
occurrences.description:
Interested in helping to care for a herd of goats in Nashville? Join our Goat Guardians team!



We manage a small herd of Tennessee fainting goats in partnership with McGavock High School where the goats live and provide educational experiences for students in the agricultural program. We're looking for volunteers to help care for our herd for the 2026-2027 school year. Whether you've worked with goats before or you're just eager to learn, we'll provide the training you need in this 2-hour session.



As a volunteer, you'll learn how to:




	
Feed and water the herd

	
Assist with daily care routines

	
Clean and maintain their living space

	
Observe goat behavior and help keep them healthy and happy





This training opportunity is for individuals who would be willing to commit 1-2 hours a day at least 2 evenings a month from September 2026-September 2027. Volunteers would continue to have guidance from members of our team for several care sessions after this initial training session to ensure comfortability. Additional training will be made available if volunteers are interested in getting more involved and learning about medical care as well as targeted grazing (goatscaping).



After completing this training session, volunteers will decide if they want to formally commit to joining our team and will then go through an onboarding process which will include the following:




	
Completing a background check

	
Getting set up with our Goat Guardians App

	
Providing additional contact info and joining our Goat Guardians group chat on Signal

The garden runs on volunteer power, no experience is necessary. Feel free to come just to learn more about gardening or share your experience.

 

Children under 12! If a parent or group will have children under the age of 12, please contact the opportunity leader below and let us know the ages in advance so we can plan activities that age group will enjoy. Children accompanying parents do not need to sign up for a spot.

 

Youth! If a group leader is signing up a group of youth under age 18, please contact the opportunity leader below before signing up.

 

As a volunteer, you may help:




	
Sow and harvest plants as needed

	
Water and weed existing garden rows

	
Prepare garden beds for planting

	
Spread wood chips around the garden





 

To prepare for volunteering:




	
Please wear closed toed shoes/boots and clothes you don't mind getting dirty.

	
We will also have all the tools you need.

occurrences.opportunityName: Urban Forestry Work Day 2026
occurrences.description:
Do you have an interest in preserving our city’s natural spaces for future generations? If so, look no further than GROW! 

 

At GROW, we are building the city’s first permaculture park space. This means we are creating an urban space where woodlands are maximized and food systems are integrated throughout the space we manage. It’s our goal to demonstrate sustainable urban food cultivation practices that maximize space, improve soils, and conserve resources such as water. 

 

Urban Forest Restoration at GROW

Covers almost 14 acres worth of the park. Both of our forest parcels have been severely affected by invasive non-native plant species. These plants ultimately have a negative impact on the wildlife that depends on this system by outcompeting native flora for resources. At GROW, we’ve taken on the ambitious task of eradicating these species and replanting native trees, shrubs, and perennials.

 

Here are some typical tasks associated with this kind of volunteer work




	
Using pruners, loppers, or Uprooter tools to remove invasive plants

	
Widening existing hiking trails by removing vegetation (thereby allowing access to new areas where we can begin reforestation efforts)

	
Spreading wood chip mulch

	
Planting new native and fruit bearing trees





Special skills you might learn or get to practice




	
Agroforestry and permaculture style farming techniques

	
Learning about various tools used for invasive plant control and Agroforestry

	
Identification of native plants and our top 3 invasive non-native plants: Bush Honeysuckle, Chinese Privet, and Euonymus vine

	
Witness goatscaping in action! This year we are bringing our goats on site to help tackle the invasive plant problem





Need-To-Knows




	
There is no running water or electricity at GROW. Volunteers should bring their own water bottles and charge their phones before arrival. 

	
There is no shelter from severe weather at GROW. In the event of severe weather on a scheduled workday (lightning, impending severe thunderstorm, or tornado watch/advisory) this event will be canceled. 

	
Volunteers should wear protective clothing appropriate for outdoor work including pants to protect legs, closed-toed shoes, breathable shirts for comfort in outdoor weather and protection from sun/brambles/stinging insects.





Parking

IMPORTANT NOTE - The address that will initially be sent after you sign up is NOT the location for this event, it is located right up the road. Please look out for an email from volunteer@growenrichment.org a few hours before the event for exact directions to our parking lot. occurrences.opportunityName: Local Legends Tour: Stage Tech Volunteer at Light the Nations Festival
occurrences.organizationServedName: Youth Empowerment Through Arts and Humanities
occurrences.managingOrganization: Youth Empowerment Through Arts and Humanities
occurrences.description:
Support Nashville’s rising youth musicians by serving as a Stage Tech Volunteer for the YEAH! Local Legends Tour, a multi‑site performance series showcasing young artists across some of the city’s legendary stages and community spaces. Stage Tech Volunteers help youth bands load in, set up, and transition smoothly between performances to help ensure every young artist feels supported, prepared, and ready to shine.



Role Overview



As a Stage Tech Volunteer, you’ll assist with load‑in and load‑out, help youth musicians get their gear set onstage, and maintain a steady flow between performances. Each event has its own unique setup and instrumentation, and YEAH! will coordinate with you ahead of time so you know exactly what to expect. All gear is provided by YEAH!.



Key Responsibilities




	
Stage setup & breakdown: Assist with loading in/out youth bands, arranging gear, and resetting the stage between acts.

	
Performer flow: Guide youth musicians on and off stage, helping them transition smoothly to the next performance.

	
Gear support: Help position amps, connect cables, place microphones, and ensure each performer is ready.

	
Event coordination: Communicate with YEAH! staff and follow the run‑of‑show for each venue.

	
Youth support: Model patience, encouragement, and professionalism while helping young performers feel confident and cared for.





Instrumentation & Prep



Instrumentation varies by event - some dates feature full youth bands, others highlight solo performers or small ensembles. YEAH! will provide info before the event outlining expected gear, performer needs, and stage layout so you can prepare confidently.



All sound and stage gear is provided by YEAH!.



Required Skills & Qualifications




	
Basic familiarity with music gear, stage setup, or live performance environments.

	
Ability to lift 25 lbs and move small gear safely.

	
Comfort working directly with youth performers.

	
Must be able to pass a background check.

	
Reliable, communicative, and committed to creating a welcoming, inclusive environment.





Volunteer Conduct & Expectations



YEAH! volunteers are ambassadors of our mission. We ask all volunteers to:




	
Treat youth, families, staff, and partners with respect, patience, and kindness.

	
Maintain a safe, substance‑free, youth‑appropriate environment.

	
Uphold YEAH!’s commitment to equity, inclusion, and belonging.

	
Communicate clearly with staff and performers.

	
Model professionalism, reliability, and positive community engagement.

	
Follow YEAH!'s Safeguarding Policy





All volunteers must complete YEAH!’s onboarding process, which includes an interview, signing a volunteer agreement, and passing a background check, when applicable. Volunteers who have not completed all required steps prior to the event date will not be eligible to participate. At this time, YEAH! is unable to accommodate volunteers seeking court‑mandated service hours.



About YEAH!



YEAH! (Youth Empowerment through Arts & Humanities) is a Nashville‑based nonprofit dedicated to empowering youth of all backgrounds through inclusive, transformative music education. Over the past 20 years, YEAH! has positively impacted more than 700 families, providing equitable access to creative opportunities that build confidence, collaboration, and community.



By volunteering for the Local Legends Tour, you help bring youth music into the heart of Nashville’s cultural spaces, amplifying young voices and strengthening community through art!

occurrences.opportunityName: Restore the Forest - Invasive Plant Removal (2026)
occurrences.organizationServedName: Friends of Shelby Park and Bottoms
occurrences.managingOrganization: Friends of Shelby Park and Bottoms
occurrences.description:
Do you love conservation? Want to work outdoors to protect the natural ecosystems of Shelby Park and Bottoms? We need you!



Shelby Park and Bottoms is a natural oasis in the heart of the city. The forests here are a refuge for people and wildlife alike. Our Shelby forests need help: they are being overtaken by invasive plant species. Through our Restore the Forest program, we remove invasive species and replant native species to revitalize a healthy forest ecosystem.



What is the community impact of this event?



Healthy forests are beautiful for park visitors, provide food and shelter for wildlife and make our local ecosystem more resilient by promoting and enhancing growth of native plant species.



What will volunteers be doing at this event?



At this event, we will be uprooting and cutting down honeysuckle and privet plants with weed wrenches, loppers, and hand saws. They will work in small groups under the supervision of experienced staff and recurring volunteers that will help teach proper plant identification and safe tool usage.



Accessibility:



This event will include hiking while carrying heavy tools over uneven ground, and we will be working off-trail within the woods. Please dress according to the weather. Porta-potties are located a short walk from our worksite, and there should always be ample parking located nearby the worksite.



What to bring?



I recommend bringing your own water bottle and sunscreen. Water, gloves, all necessary tools, and additional water will be provided. Please wear sturdy shoes that are good for gardening (e.g. hiking boots), long socks, and long pants to protect yourselves from sticks and thorns in the forest. If possible, long sleeved shirts can also be helpful for protection, but please dress according to the weather.



What’s next?



If you sign up for this event, you will receive a reminder email a few days before the event with specific instructions regarding parking and any other necessary information.





Founded in 2008, Friends of Shelby is a private, nonprofit organization working to preserve, enhance, and promote Shelby Park and Bottoms for everyone to appreciate and protect. We work to protect the natural and historical integrity of the area by supporting appropriate recreational activities, maintaining and enhancing its features, promoting programs that inspire appreciation and conservation of the Park and Bottoms, and advocating for a level playing field for the various user groups.
